question: Confidence-band evidence for back-office AI: find 2021+ field or audit studies that report, for an AI system with a confidence threshold, the share of cases auto-closed and the error rate inside the auto-closed band (KYC/AML alert disposition, invoice/AP matching, document classification). Target the full texts of E15 (alert prevalence, so the 80% false-positive cut can be turned into a per-closed-alert miss rate) and E17 (Choi & Xie: intervention rates by confidence score)
conclusion_affected: Routing variant of C: h (share of AI-amenable cases routed to AI alone) and e (excess error in that band) are evidence-bounded only by radiology (E19) and one bank's ML triage (E15)
rationale: h ~ U(0.21, 0.49) rests on one radiology paper and e ~ U(0, 0.10) on two endpoints; at m = 20 the routing pool falls below the assist pool, so the escaped-error cost and e decide whether routing beats assistance

question: Cost of an escaped back-office error at a DAF sponsor: from public enforcement, audit and complaint records (state AG settlements, IRS excise-tax cases under §4966/§4967, sponsor grant-reversal and void policies), estimate the handling-cost multiple m of an error that a sampled QA pass would have caught (misdirected grant, grant to a non-qualifying recipient, duplicate payment)
conclusion_affected: Whether routing (AI-only closure) pays: the large-national routing pool is $1.36m at m=1, $1.06m at m=5 and $44k at m=20
rationale: m has no public source; it is shown only as a sweep [I]. It moves the routing value pool more than any other routing parameter

question: Re-cut the redesign (D) and conventional-automation (B) ranges with the same evidence standard as C. Routing raises C's value pool about threefold at a large national but leaves P(C ranks first) near 1%, because D and B still dominate gross value; the B/D parameters (d_p, beta, b_p) are v1 assumptions never calibrated
conclusion_affected: The A/B/C/D ranking; whether 'AI is weak' is a statement about AI or about uncalibrated B/D priors
rationale: After routing, C's weakness in ranking comes from the comparison set, not from the assist formula: the modal winner changes in no process (0 of 15 at every archetype and scenario)

question: Grant-level recipient data for one large sponsor: obtain a public grant-level listing (some sponsors publish grant search or annual grant lists; state charity registries; nonprofit-side receipts) to measure grants per recipient against recipient dollars directly, replacing the swept beta in n_i = max(1, k d_i^beta)
conclusion_affected: Per-grant exception share: broad union 17-31% of grants depending on beta; core 7-8.5% is stable
rationale: beta is the only unidentified assumption; Fidelity's count of $1m+ grants is matched only for beta <= 0.35 under the line-mean approximation, and NPT's published international-grant share (0.31%) sits below every beta

question: Reconcile NPT's Schedule F foreign recipient counts (413 in FY2023, 488 in FY2024) with its annual report's international grant counts (335 and 406, U.S. DAF program only): which NPT entities, programs or region rows sit in the 990 count, and is the Schedule F 'recipient' count larger than the grant count?
conclusion_affected: Foreign share by grant (0.31% published vs 1.2-8% modelled from Schedule F)
rationale: The 990 reports more foreign recipients than the annual report reports international grants, so Schedule F counts cannot be read as grant counts

question: Annual grant counts for the other top-50 sponsors: DAFgiving360 (robots.txt returns HTTP 403, so not fetched), Schwab Charitable (same), BofA CGF and Renaissance (no e-file Schedule I), American Endowment Foundation and NCF (impact reports state dollars and charities but no grant count); request a permitted access route or find a mirrored copy of the FY2023-24 counts
conclusion_affected: Coverage of the per-grant estimate (now 6 sponsors in pools: Fidelity; NPT; Vanguard; Goldman Sachs; Ayco; T. Rowe Price)
rationale: DAFgiving360 is the second-largest grant-maker by count; its absence leaves the pooled per-grant share dominated by Fidelity (about 88% of pooled report-sponsor grants)
